messages.subject: exact log Marginal likelihood
parts:
To the INLA proficient coder

I am looking at the example in RW1 documentation:

n=100
z=seq(0,6,length.out=n)
y=sin(z)+rnorm(n,mean=0,sd=0.5)
data=data.frame(y=y,z=z)

formula=y~f(z,model="rw1",
            hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01))))

result=inla(formula,data=data,family="gaussian")


When I ran this code I get:

> Marginal log-Likelihood:  -242.05

But the documentation also states that "The term 1/2 log(|R|∗) of the normalization constant is not computed, hence you need to add this part to the log marginal likelihood estimate, if you need it."


I am not sure what |R|∗  is...?

I need to get the actual marginal log-likelihood so i can compare its estimate with the one of another model (DIC and WAIC point to a different model and I am hoping that the log mLik will help in choosing).


Thank you for your help


Saba

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] exact log Marginal likelihood
parts:
Hi,

for the intrinsic models, like RW1, RW2, BESAG, etc, the determinant of
the precision matrix's part of the normalizing constant is not
included. |A|^* is the 'generalized' determinant, like the determinant
of the nonsingular part of A, or simply the product of all non-zero
eigenvalues.

For DIC, WAIC, this constant is not needed, only if you happen to
compare marginal likelihood with and without a RW2 term, f.ex.

H
